# The Human Internet: Design System

The source of truth for every value is `design-system/tokens.json` in the web repo. `node design-system/build.mjs` generates the web CSS, iOS `DesignTokens.swift`, Android `DesignTokens.kt`, and the front matter of this file, and copies this file into all three repos. Don't hand-edit those generated files. This file explains the intent behind the values; the tokens hold the values themselves. Tokens come from the brand guide ("Brand Scroller, light version", by Syrens) plus measurements of the UI and motion in the scroller.

## Overview

**Concept: The Human Imprint.** The identity puts the human imprint at the center and makes authorship visible on an internet increasingly shaped by AI.

Three ideas carry the whole brand:

1. **A quiet canvas for loud humans.** The interface is predominantly white and spacious. Creators' photos are the only rich color on screen, and the UI steps back.
2. **One imperfect mark.** The spiral "imprint" is organic, slightly irregular, and never quite the same twice. It is the only hand-made shape in an otherwise precise system, and it means *a real human did this*.
3. **Plain, confident words.** Short declarative sentences, often in pairs: "Made by a human. Signed by a phone." / "Photo verified. Go show them."

Personality: warm, direct, a little wry. The UI isn't techy, crypto-ish, or security-themed, even though the product is cryptography.

## Colors

The palette is black, white, and one light gray. That restraint is the brand.

- **Background `#FFFFFF`**: every page canvas.
- **Surface `#F6F6F6`**: cards, info panels, icon buttons, and the selfie frame's surroundings. Use fill to separate content, not borders or shadows.
- **Foreground `#000000`**: all primary text, the mark, and primary buttons.
- **Muted foreground `#666666`**: labels, metadata, timestamps, and coordinates. The scroller mockups use a lighter `#8F8F8F`, but that fails WCAG AA for small text, so it is kept as `subtle-foreground` for text 18px and up or decorative text only. The verification page has an accessibility requirement, so muted text there must always be `#666666`.
- **Highlight `#91CDFF`**: the one chromatic UI color, seen on the streak badge. Use it only for small count/achievement badges, with black text. It never appears on buttons, links, or large areas.
- **Destructive `#C0281C`**: *proposed, not in the brand guide.* Use it for form errors and destructive confirmations only.

Color in the product comes from **photography**, never from the UI.

## Typography

**Neue Montreal, Medium (500)**, with Inter Display as the fallback named in the brand guide. Everything uses one weight. Show hierarchy through **size** and **color** (black vs. muted gray), never through bold.

- Headlines are large, tightly tracked, and tightly leaded (`display`, `h1`). Let them be big. A two-line headline with a period at the end is the signature layout.
- The **label/value pair** is the core text pattern: a muted label above a black value (e.g. "Photo verified" / "Go show them.", "Weekly Streak" / "Hard to miss you now.").
- Proof metadata (device, date, OS, location) is set in `title` size, black, with the secondary part (time, coordinates) inline in `caption` size and muted.
- Use sentence case everywhere in the UI. The wordmark is always lowercase: **the human ~ internet**.

## Layout

- Use a 4px base unit. Default to generous whitespace: when unsure, add space rather than a divider.
- Mobile-first with a single column. Center the wordmark at the top of app screens.
- Page sections are separated by `24` (96px) on desktop and `16` (64px) on mobile.
- Content is centered with a comfortable max width of about 1200px for marketing pages and about 440px for app flows.
- Photos lead. Give them the most area on the screen and keep them uncropped where possible.

## Elevation & Depth

The system is flat. Separate layers with fill (`surface` on `background`), not lines or shadows.

- Cards have no shadow and no border.
- Only truly floating things (popovers, sheets, a browser-window mockup) get `shadow-float`, a single soft, wide, low-opacity shadow.
- **Frosted reveal**: on a verified photo, hover or tap blurs the image behind a translucent white layer and reveals the proof metadata. This is the signature interaction (see Motion).

## Shapes

- Corners are soft: cards and photos use `lg` (16px), info panels use `md` (12px), and large hero photos use `xl`–`2xl`.
- Buttons and icon buttons are fully round (pills and circles).
- The selfie / identity-verification frame is a tall rounded "pebble": `rounded-2xl` on a portrait box, not a hard circle or rectangle.
- **The mark is the only irregular shape.** Never draw other blobby or wobbly UI shapes; that would dilute it.

## Motion

Values were measured frame by frame from the brand scroller video.

- **Brand reveal**: elements fade in by opacity only, over about 750ms with a gentle decelerate (`ease-out`). Sequential elements are staggered by about 800ms. The wordmark reveals "the" → "human" + mark → "internet". There is no sliding, scaling, or bouncing.
- **Frosted proof reveal**: hovering a verified photo crossfades to the frosted metadata state in about 300ms, and fades back in about 300ms.
- **The mark "boils"**: the spiral is redrawn slightly differently every ~120ms (~8fps, stepped, no easing), like hand-drawn animation. It alternates every few seconds between solid black and filled with a flipbook of real photos. Use this only on brand moments (splash, landing hero, the success state after verification), never on routine UI.
- **Exit**: a quick wipe or fade of about 250ms.
- UI micro-interactions (press, toggle) use `duration-fast` (150ms).
- `prefers-reduced-motion` disables all of it. Reveals become instant and the mark holds still.

## Components

Start from shadcn/ui primitives restyled with these tokens, then use these brand components:

- **Button**: there are three CTA roles. Primary is a black pill, secondary is a light-gray pill, and tertiary is text only (black, no fill), for low-emphasis actions like "Not now". Use at most one primary per screen. Labels are short verbs ("Share", "Copy link", "Download on the App Store").
- **IconButton**: a 48px light-gray circle with a single outline icon (lucide, 1.5px stroke).
- **VerifiedMark**: the spiral mark at small size. It is *the* verification symbol. Pair it with copy ("Your photo was successfully verified!"). Never use a green check or shield.
- **ProofCard**: a photo with the frosted reveal, followed by an info card with label/value metadata and a share/copy-link card beside it.
- **NotificationCard**: a light-gray rounded card holding a square white thumbnail (photo or doodle) and a label/value text pair, with an optional corner badge (VerifiedMark or highlight count).
- **ProfileHeader**: avatar plus VerifiedMark overlap, name in `title` size, and a muted meta line ("Influencer · Joined 2026 · 84 verified photos").
- **Doodle**: a black hand-drawn line illustration on white (pointing hand, flame). Use it for empty states and notification thumbnails, at no more than one per view.
- **Wordmark**: `/public/brand/wordmark.svg`, centered in the app header. **Mark**: `/public/brand/mark.svg`.

## Do's and Don'ts

**Do**
- Let real photos provide all the color.
- Use one weight and create hierarchy with size and gray.
- Write in short, declarative, two-beat lines with periods.
- Use the spiral mark as the signal for "verified / human".
- Meet WCAG AA, especially on the verification flow.

**Don't**
- Add brand colors, gradients, or colored buttons. Blue is for badges only.
- Use bold, all caps, or more than one weight.
- Use a check mark, shield, lock, or padlock to mean "verified".
- Use stock or AI-generated imagery. Every image must look candidly human-made.
- Use bouncy, springy, or sliding animation, or put shadows on cards.
- Stretch, recolor, outline, or re-draw the mark, or set the wordmark in caps.

## Platforms

The rules above are the same everywhere. Only the implementation differs:

| | Web | iOS | Android |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tokens (generated) | `app/tokens.css` → Tailwind via `globals.css` | `DesignSystem/DesignTokens.swift`, read by `Theme.swift` / `Typography.swift` | `designsystem/DesignTokens.kt`, read by `HumanTheme.kt` |
| Components | shadcn/ui + `src/components/brand` | `DesignSystem/Components.swift` | `designsystem/BrandComponents.kt` (Material 3 restyled) |
| Type sizes | `fontSize` column | mobile sizes, scaled with Dynamic Type | mobile sizes in `sp` (scales with system font size) |
| Icons | lucide, 1.5px stroke | SF Symbols, `.light` / `.regular` weight | Material Symbols **Outlined**, weight 300 |
| Font | Inter Display (Neue Montreal when licensed) | Inter Display TTFs bundled; Neue Montreal behind `neue_font` flag | Inter Display in `res/font`; same flag |
| Reduced motion | `prefers-reduced-motion` | `accessibilityReduceMotion` | `animator duration scale = 0` |
| Haptics | none | soft impact on capture and on "Photo verified" | `HapticFeedbackType.Confirm` at the same moments |
| Styleguide | `/styleguide` route | `DesignSystemStyleguide.swift` `#Preview` | `StyleguideScreen.kt` `@Preview` |

On mobile, the mobile type scale applies (display 44, h1 34, h2 28, h3 22, title 18, body 16, label 14, caption 12). Android's minimum touch target is 48dp; iOS's is 44pt.

The three styleguides should show the same components in the same order, so "build it like the ProofCard" means the same thing on every platform.
